results.snippet:
Bipedal humanoid devices that used to cost hundreds of thousands of yuan and only appeared on exhibition stages are now being put on shelves on e-commerce platforms in batches, and products priced at the ten-thousand-yuan level have broken the public's price expectation for humanoid robots.
...
Since the second half of 2025, the situation has begun to undergo fundamental changes.
Many domestic manufacturers have successively released mass-produced models that support spot goods or scheduled delivery, and humanoid robots have officially entered the sales stage for individual consumers.
...
Chinese manufacturers account for more than 97% of the share, and Agibot and Unitree together account for three-quarters of the global shipment.
...
>
Songyan Power's "Bumi" is priced at 9,998 yuan, bringing bipedal humanoid robots into the range below 10,000 yuan for the first time; Unitree Robotics' Unitree R1 was reduced from 39,900 yuan to a starting price of 29,900 yuan for spot sale, and it topped the humanoid robot sales list on JD.com just one week later;
Ubtech's U1 series covers a price range from 119,800 yuan to 990,000 yuan, taking the "emotional companionship" route; Agibot Lingxi X2 Youth Edition is priced at 98,000 yuan, and the accelerated evolution Booster K1 Education Edition is 66,900 yuan; even industrial-grade products are exploring the lowest price range.
Stardust Intelligence's T1 has a starting price as low as 89,900 yuan, claiming to be the "Chinese version of Figure".
Among them, Unitree Robotics is the landmark player in this round of price cuts for consumer-grade humanoid robots.
Its R1 humanoid robot was originally priced at 39,900 yuan, and was lowered to a starting price of 29,900 yuan in June 2026.
This robot focuses on lightweight bipedal walking and basic obstacle avoidance, supports secondary development for developers, can complete standing up, walking, jumping, following and basic gesture interaction, and is oriented at individual players, university laboratories and science and innovation enthusiasts.
...
It is worth mentioning that **when manufacturers turn their sights to the C-end, the industry begins to replicate the gameplay of consumer electronics**: dividing basic version, youth version and developer version, launching online pre-sales, deposit-locking orders, offline experience stores, opening official stores on Douyin, Tmall and JD.com, and directly selling to individual consumers.
...
Qiyuan Robotics opened its first global store on Huaihai Middle Road in Shanghai, and the first batch of delivered Q1 and T1 are priced from 19,999 yuan.

content.text:
Several humanoid robots can be ordered in Asia, particularly from Chinese manufacturers. Availability ranges from consumer and education models to costly enterprise systems; “available” may mean preorder, quote-based procurement, or reseller listing—not necessarily immediate local stock.

Examples with published prices include:

- **Unitree R1** — listed at about **US$9,990** by an Asia-focused seller; Chinese reporting also gives a domestic starting price of **¥29,900**.[4][10]
- **Unitree G1** — around **US$16,000** through sellers listing it for sale.[3][6]
- **Noetix BUMI** — consumer/education models listed at roughly **US$4,995–14,995**.[5]
- **UBTECH Walker** — industrial and service models listed from about **US$37,500**, with some variants priced much higher.[1]
- **EngineAI T800** — listed from about **US$40,500**.[4]
- **RobotEra Q5** — wheeled humanoid service robot listed at about **US$63,000**.[8]
- **LimX Oli** — full-size humanoid with an order/consultation route; public pricing is limited, though one reseller lists an education version at **US$72,000**.[9]
- **AiMOGA Mornine M1**, **Galbot S1**, and **UBTECH Cruzr** — also appear on Asia-focused seller listings, with Cruzr a wheeled service robot rather than a biped.[2][4]

Treat marketplace and reseller prices as indicative: verify the seller, regional delivery, import duties, warranty, support, and whether the robot is actually in stock before ordering. Some listings may be enterprise-only or quote-based.
